ayahs.text_arabic: صِرَاطَ الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا الضَّالِّينَ
ayahs.text_transliteration: Sirat al-ladhina an'amta 'alayhim ghayri al-maghdubi 'alayhim wa la al-dhallin
ayahs.context: Al-Fatiha, the opening surah; Path of the Blessed
ayahs.ibn_kathir_excerpt: The path of those whom God has favored - meaning the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous. This refers to following the way of those whom God has blessed with guidance and obedience. The scholars agree that this includes the Prophet and his companions.
ayahs.maududi_excerpt: The Straight Path means the way of life that leads to success and salvation. It is the path of those whom God has blessed - those who have been guided to truth and righteousness. This excludes those upon whom His wrath has descended (those who knew truth but rejected it) and those who went astray (who were in ignorance).
ayahs.tabari_excerpt: Some scholars say the blessed ones are the believers and the righteous servants. Others say it refers specifically to the believers in God's oneness. The majority of the scholars agree this means those who have received God's favors of knowledge and obedience.
ayahs.scholarly_notes: This ayah is recited in every unit of prayer. Classical tafsir commentators emphasize the distinction between those who actively rejected truth (maghdub) versus those in ignorance (dhallin). Modern scholars apply this to ethical and spiritual guidance in contemporary context.

ayahs.text_arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الصِّيَامُ
ayahs.text_transliteration: Ya ayyuha alladhina amanu kutiba 'alaykum al-siyam
ayahs.context: Surah al-Baqarah; Fasting in Ramadan is ordained
ayahs.ibn_kathir_excerpt: The obligation of fasting has been decreed for you, as it was decreed for those before you. Fasting (sawm) means to refrain from food, drink, and sexual relations from dawn until sunset. This is one of the pillars of Islam.
ayahs.maududi_excerpt: Fasting has been prescribed for you as it was prescribed for the believers before you, so that you may become God-conscious. Fasting is not merely abstinence from food; it is a discipline that trains the soul and develops piety. The mention of those before you (previous nations) emphasizes the universality of this obligation.
ayahs.tabari_excerpt: Fasting is obligatory upon you - meaning it is binding and necessary. This obligation was established for the previous nations as well. The purpose of fasting is that you might attain taqwa (God-consciousness and fear).
ayahs.scholarly_notes: Classical scholars unanimously agree on the obligation of fasting during Ramadan. Juristic schools (madhabs) differ on specific exceptions and compensatory measures (qada and fidya). Medical and situational exemptions are detailed in the following verses.

ayahs.ibn_kathir_excerpt: Every soul shall taste death - this is a fundamental reality that applies to all creatures without exception. Even the prophets and the righteous must face death. This is a reminder of the transience of worldly life and the permanence of the afterlife.
ayahs.maududi_excerpt: Every living soul will inevitably experience death. This is an established law of God from which none can escape, regardless of their status or wealth. The purpose of mentioning this is to prepare people for the reality of accountability in the afterlife and to encourage righteous actions.
ayahs.tabari_excerpt: No living being can escape death. Both the good and the evil, the noble and the common, will taste death. This verse serves as a reminder that worldly life is temporary and the real life is the life to come.
ayahs.scholarly_notes: This ayah appears multiple times in the Quran and is considered a foundational concept in Islamic theology regarding life, death, and the afterlife. It is often cited in discussions of mawt (death) and the intermediate realm (barzakh).

ayahs.context: Surah al-Nisa; Family structure and responsibility
ayahs.ibn_kathir_excerpt: Men are the protectors and maintainers of women because God has given them superiority and because they spend their wealth on women. The righteous women are therefore obedient, guarding the unseen as God has guarded. The scholar emphasizes this is regarding financial obligation and leadership, not personal virtue.
ayahs.maududi_excerpt: Men have been placed as protectors and maintainers over women due to the qualities God has given them and the obligations He has placed on them financially. This leadership is a trust and comes with responsibility. Women have corresponding rights and protections. This does not diminish women's other roles, rights, and responsibilities.
ayahs.tabari_excerpt: Men are responsible for the care and protection of women because of the qualities God has given them - referring to physical strength and the economic obligations placed upon them. This is a discussion of roles and responsibilities within the family structure as ordained by God.
ayahs.scholarly_notes: This is among the most discussed ayahs regarding gender relations in Islam. Scholars emphasize that qawwam refers to financial responsibility and guardianship, not absolute authority. Women's rights to education, property, business, and consent are detailed elsewhere in Islamic law. Different contexts and interpretations across madhabs.

ayahs.text_arabic: مِنْ أَجْلِ ذَلِكَ كَتَبْنَا عَلَىٰ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ أَنَّهُ مَن قَتَلَ نَفْسًا بِغَيْرِ نَفْسٍ أَوْ فَسَادٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ
ayahs.text_transliteration: Min ajl dhalika katabna 'ala bani isra'il annahu man qatala nafs bi-ghayri nafs aw fasad fi al-ard
ayahs.ibn_kathir_excerpt: We prescribed upon the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul - except for a soul, or for corruption upon the earth - it is as if he had slain all of mankind. Conversely, whoever saves a life is as if he had saved all of mankind. The Prophet explained that this ruling includes both the Torah and Islamic Law.
ayahs.maududi_excerpt: This law was revealed to the Children of Israel and is also part of Islamic teaching. The taking of an innocent life is an exceptionally grave sin. The only exceptions to this prohibition are lawful execution by authority for capital crimes and legitimate defense against aggression. The parallel positive statement elevates the value of preserving life.
ayahs.tabari_excerpt: The people of Israel were commanded that killing a soul without just cause is among the gravest sins. The exceptions are: (1) legal punishment for capital crimes, (2) defense against aggression, (3) preventing greater harm. The verse emphasizes the oneness of humanity in the value of human life.
ayahs.scholarly_notes: This verse is foundational in Islamic ethics regarding the sanctity of life. Medieval scholars extensively discussed the conditions and exceptions. Modern Islamic scholars frequently cite this in bioethical discussions and contemporary peace-building contexts. Unanimous agreement on the gravity of unjustified killing.
